MOTION STUDIO · SOFTWARE CHANGE REPORT · 11 November 2026

One setup before every round.

Video and game-specific options now share a separate menu in Mole Motion and Dodgeball. It opens on load, on Set up round, on Play again and for identity-recovery restarts.

Issue #33 · Review pull request

What changed and why

The permanent sidebar became a native dialog with Video & input and Game settings sections. This keeps related decisions together and gives the game the full content width. Existing options, including Touch/Flick/Push, and camera ownership remain in the app; game engines still own collisions and scoring. The integration preserves the diagnostic and wrist-flick features merged into main at 3a4337f.

  • Opening or closing setup without editing choices retains the current results. Only explicit Start round confirmation resets the score and records start intent. Every new round returns through that confirmation.
  • Selections stay in the existing controls between rounds. Active play locks configuration; required identity recovery allows a new setup. Pause/Resume stay in the play view.
  • Camera capture still requires Start camera. Stop, release errors and retry are available inside setup and on the operator page. Both surfaces call the same epoch-scoped release controller.
  • The native modal keeps keyboard focus inside setup, starts with focus on Close, supports Escape, and restores the requesting control. Phone options scroll between a persistent header and Start action.

The extra confirmation before replay is deliberate: each new round gets a chance to review video and game settings. Resume continues an existing round without this step. No new dependency, distributable package, inference path or wire contract is introduced; the CI component/build table remains current.
